roadmap.goal: Story 6459 (T1): the backend test run keeps its memory flat. Disposed test hosts are released instead of being pinned by static timers. Two roots are removed: (1) the OAuth providers hold a factory-made HTTP client for the life of the host, which keeps the client factory's cleanup timer looping; (2) the rate limiters' replenishment timers are never stopped when the host is disposed (the one-address global limiter, and the framework middleware's private endpoint limiter). Rate limiting stays ON with the same rules. A leak guard in the test project (cases A, B, C) fails if a disposed host stays reachable. Target (the only one): peak memory of a full standard-filter run under 3 GB and flat, measured before and after by the lead.

phases.description: One slice, two serial steps (01-01 then 01-02), owned by the crafter, profile standard, in the main checkout. Preconditions P0, P-final and the closing mutation run are owned by the lead (see roadmap preconditions). Measured in DESIGN: neither the OAuth change nor the rate-limiter change frees any host alone, so 01-01 turns no leak-guard case green and ALL [Ignore] attributes on TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest (cases A, B, C) come off together in 01-02, the first change that frees a host. The guard fixture and its allowlist entry in BackendTestParallelizationGuardTest are already committed (DISTILL). Nothing is pushed. Each commit is focused and green on its own; refactor commits are separate from feature commits. Git commands prefixed LEAN_CTX_DISABLED=1. Run only the filtered test classes named per step; the full standard-filter run belongs to the lead. Standard filter: TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration. Rules for all code in both steps: (a) comments are rare, written for a stranger, and never cite internal references (no story, decision, ADR, slice or scenario ids such as D1b, A2, ADR-005, AC-5.2); the reason goes in plain language or in the commit body. (b) No nWave scenario tags in code or test names (no @us-, @slice-, @kpi-, @contract-shape, @walking_skeleton, @driving_port, @error, @real-io); test names are plain language. (c) Read docs/ci-learnings.md (backend section) before writing code; the build promotes Sonar and Roslyn rules to errors, so `dotnet build` must finish with zero warnings. (d) The ArchUnit rules in the test project must stay green. (e) The product-side behaviour of routes, DTOs, responses and rate-limit rules is unchanged.

steps.name: OAuth providers ask IHttpClientFactory per request; test hosts shorten the handler lifetime
steps.description: Commit type: `fix(oauth): ask the HTTP client factory per token request instead of holding a client`. Change JiraOAuthProvider and AdoOAuthProvider so the constructor takes IHttpClientFactory (the client name constant HttpClientName is already public on each class) instead of an HttpClient, and each token request asks the factory for the named client at the point of use. Do not dispose the client in a way that disposes the pooled handler (the factory owns the handler). Change the two singleton registrations in Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/Program.cs (around lines 1526-1542) into plain type registrations (AddSingleton<JiraOAuthProvider>() style, resolved through the container); leave the AddHttpClient(name, 30 s timeout) registrations (around 356-364) and the 2-minute product handler lifetime (around 340-343) untouched. Arrange-only test edits (assertions unchanged): JiraOAuthProviderTest.CreateProvider, AdoOAuthProviderTest.CreateProvider and OAuthServiceTest.ArrangeRefreshThroughARealIdentityProvider each build a Mock<IHttpClientFactory> whose CreateClient(<Provider>.HttpClientName) returns a fresh `new HttpClient(handler, disposeHandler: false)` on every call (a function, not a shared instance; disposeHandler:false so one request's `using` cannot dispose the stub handler the next request needs) and pass factory.Object. In OAuthServiceTest the handler is the real identity provider; RequestCountingHandler assertions stay. No new shared helper. In Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/TestHelpers/TestWebApplicationFactory.cs add a test-only re-registration of the client factory's handler lifetime to 1 second (ConfigureAll<HttpClientFactoryOptions> applied after the product's registration) with a plain-language comment on why (a host that really used a client stays pinned until the lifetime plus the factory's fixed 10 s cleanup tick; no test relies on connection reuse). This step turns NO leak-guard case green; report that as measured, do not claim otherwise, and do not remove any [Ignore] here. Gates: `dotnet build` with 0 warnings; run only the three OAuth classes (filter FullyQualifiedName~JiraOAuthProviderTest|FullyQualifiedName~AdoOAuthProviderTest|FullyQualifiedName~OAuthServiceTest) plus the OAuth controller and registry tests, and record the passed/failed counts per class.

steps.name: Rate-limiter seam: container-owned limiters, own construction of the middleware, leak guard enabled
steps.description: Commit type: `fix(rate-limiting): dispose the rate limiters with the host and guard against leaked test hosts` (the crafter may split ADR/docs and Stryker config into trailing docs commits if each stays green). FIRST read the framework's UseRateLimiter source for the pinned .NET version (RateLimiterApplicationBuilderExtensions in Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting, via the pinned SDK/shared-framework version or the dotnet/aspnetcore tag that matches `dotnet --version`) and record what it does, expecting: a check that AddRateLimiter's services are registered (it throws otherwise) and UseMiddleware<RateLimitingMiddleware>. Preserve BOTH in our replacement: the services-registered check with an equivalent failure, and the pipeline position. Then: (1) Create a container-owned rate-limiter owner class (suggested name RateLimiterOwner; final name is the crafter's, and the Stryker config is edited to match). It owns the one-address global limiter (the existing WhatOneAddressMayHandIn body, moved not edited: same partitions, same numbers) and is registered as a DI singleton so the container disposes it with the host; the limiter reaches RateLimiterOptions.GlobalLimiter through an IConfigureOptions<RateLimiterOptions> registration instead of being created inline in the AddRateLimiter block. (2) The owner also receives the framework middleware instance we construct and, in Dispose, disposes the middleware's private `_endpointLimiter` field (type PartitionedRateLimiter<HttpContext>) by reflection. (3) In Program.cs replace `app.UseRateLimiter()` (about line 216) with our own construction of the internal RateLimitingMiddleware: look the type up by name in the Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting assembly, create it the way UseMiddleware does (ActivatorUtilities.CreateInstance with the next delegate; its public constructor takes RequestDelegate, ILogger<RateLimitingMiddleware>, IOptions<RateLimiterOptions>, IServiceProvider, RateLimitingMetrics in .NET 10), hand the instance to the owner, and return a RequestDelegate bound to its Invoke. Keep the SAME `RateLimits:Enabled` gate and the SAME pipeline position (between the same neighbours as today). Unconditional, not test-gated: one code path. (4) The reflection lookup is separated so a unit test can hand it a type to inspect. If the internal type, its constructor, its Invoke method or the `_endpointLimiter` field is missing, startup throws a message that names the missing member and says to re-read the framework's RateLimitingMiddleware source after a .NET upgrade; rate limiting is never silently skipped. (5) Fail-loud unit tests in the SAME commit as the owner class, one per missing member: type, constructor, Invoke, `_endpointLimiter`; each hands the lookup a type lacking exactly that member and asserts the exception message names that member and mentions the .NET upgrade (plain NUnit tests, plain names, no scenario tags; suggested file RateLimiterOwnerTest.cs next to the owner's other tests; they also serve the mutation run). (6) In TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest.cs remove ALL THREE [Ignore] attributes together (case A AHostThatServedARequestIsFreedOnceDisposed, case B AHostThatResolvedEveryOAuthProviderIsFreedOnceDisposed, case C AHostThatCreatedOneHttpClientIsFreedOnceDisposed). Case C may only be un-ignored because 01-01's one-second handler lifetime is already in TestWebApplicationFactory (an earlier commit). Leave the tests' assertions as written; do not weaken, shorten or skip them. If a case does not go green, stop and report with the printed failure rather than adjusting the assertion; an abandoned fix removes the scaffold rather than leaving it skipped. (7) Docs in the same change: add a short addendum to docs/product/architecture/adr-005-rate-limiting-middleware.md (own construction of the middleware, container-owned disposal of both limiters, reflection with a fail-loud startup, and the check to run on every .NET major upgrade and any minor touching Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting); read ARCHITECTURE.md's rate-limiting text (today it names rate limiting only as an API-edge concern around section 4, line ~297) and update it in the same step ONLY if it describes how the middleware is constructed, otherwise record 'checked, no change, because ...'. ADR-270 needs no change (no context, term, edge or event); state that. (8) Fix docs/feature/story-6459-t1-backend-test-memory-flat/mutation/stryker-config.story-6459.json: the `mutate` glob `**/*RateLimiterOwner*.cs` and the `test-case-filter` term `FullyQualifiedName~RateLimiterOwner` must match the real owner file and its real test class names (keep the two provider files in both; keep the acceptance-suite exclusions). Verify the corrected names with ctx_search; the Stryker run itself is the lead's gate. (9) Gates, with counts recorded: `dotnet build` 0 warnings; run the four rate-limit classes S6_RateLimitingTests, UsageDataConsentRateLimitTests, Slice11CastAVoteScenarios and UsageDataEventCeilingTests plus the three OAuth classes JiraOAuthProviderTest, AdoOAuthProviderTest and OAuthServiceTest, all green; run the guard fixture alone with `dotnet test -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest"` FIVE consecutive times and record each result and duration (this is what confirms the Release-build claim that Release roots the same timers as Debug); confirm from a log (--logger "console;verbosity=detailed") that the [NonParallelizable] fixture ran alone; also run once the two parallelization-guard tests in BackendTestParallelizationGuardTest; ctx_search shows no `[Ignore` left in TestHostIsReleasedAfterDisposeTest.cs. (10) Read-only Renovate/branch-protection check: `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection` (or the rulesets API) to see whether the backend tests are required checks; record the result in feature-delta.md under `## Wave: DELIVER / [REF] Evidence step 01-02`; if they are not required, record it as a risk for the maintainer and change nothing. Also record in that section: the UseRateLimiter source findings, the counts, the five Release run results and the NonParallelizable log evidence. Never run the unfiltered suite and never run another backend suite concurrently.

steps.implementation_notes: Variant 5 of the DESIGN spike is the measured shape: host dies with the global limiter owned by the container and the endpoint limiter disposed by the owner; SuppressFlow alone fails (second path through the middleware closure), and no public API releases the endpoint limiter. In .NET 10 the middleware fields are _next, _defaultOnRejected, _logger, _metrics, _globalLimiter, _endpointLimiter, _rejectionStatusCode, _policyMap, _defaultPolicyKey; only _endpointLimiter is disposed by us (the global limiter is ours). Contract shape of the owner: bounded-change, universe = this host's two limiters; the reflection edge is a driven-side adapter whose failure is loud at startup, which is every WebApplicationFactory test and every app start. Capability: the owner receives only what it disposes (the middleware instance), not the service provider. The guard's own mechanics (warm-up host, synchronous NoInlining creation method, GC polling, S1215 pragma with a reason) already exist; do not rewrite them. Polling limit on CI is an open question: if the first CI run flakes, raise the limit, never drop the assertion (the lead handles that after push). Because Program.cs changes, the push triggers the full Integration suite in CI; the lead announces it. Out of this step and owned by the lead: one full standard-filter run with rate limiting on, green apart from the 2 known publish-output scan failures, with the guard passing once inside that run (not run concurrently with another backend suite); P-final measurement and the tail monitor; the Stryker run on the two provider files and the owner class (read the per-file table, kill rate >= 80%, survivors killed or justified).
